author: NorthEast News Desk
body: New Hampshire Public Radio has released a Concord conversation with two-time Pulitzer Prize-winning author Colson Whitehead focused on “Cool Machine,” the third and final novel in his Harlem trilogy.

The installment returns to Ray Carney, the series’ salesman by day and fence by night, while using his story to examine a changing New York City. NHPR said the discussion explored the novel’s questions about morality, ownership and whether theft committed in response to injustice can be judged in simple terms.

The interview was recorded July 24 at the Capitol Center for the Arts as part of NHPR’s Authors on Main series. Julia Barnett and Olivia Comolli presented the program, which was published Wednesday as an audio conversation for listeners across New Hampshire.

The release gives Granite State readers a regional entry point into the conclusion of Whitehead’s multigenerational crime saga. Authors on Main brings writers to Concord for public discussions, while NHPR Books airs Saturdays and distributes its conversations through major podcast platforms. The station also maintains an archive of earlier literary interviews and coverage.

headline: Colson Whitehead discusses final Harlem novel in Concord program
